title: Can bond distances still identify the next joins with the original eight attached?
claim: Two legally reachable mixed presentations on the same 36 observed distinctions have identical complete allowed states but opposite next-round feasibility under the original simultaneous rule. The full anonymous scalar bond-distance table cannot determine the next joins.
standard_statement: Determine whether legal transition options for a finite binary constraint presentation are equivariant under all isometries of its minimum-support pair table. An allowed-state symmetry or two identical relations that change those options refutes identifiability.
prior_work: The pure parity inverse explicitly excludes the nonlinear eight-place restriction. The original cubic construction gives the attachment and both growth policies.
completion_gate: All-stage proof or a checked counterexample on the same current distinctions. Distinguish exact selections from synchronous feasibility and guaranteed cubic histories.

validation.status: Exact finite witnesses checked with the original growth policy, constructive per-row enumeration and independent same-task review.
validation.independence: Separate within-task algorithms for the state relation: parameterized elimination with explicit fresh truth tables, and constructive generation from the original betweennesses with per-row lifts. The capacity reconstruction and a concrete allocation are compared against the archived predecessor policy. The shortest-support checks use the canonical knot CLI.

source_contribution: The literal old eight-place betweenness relation, its attachment, and the serial and simultaneous parity growth rules are supplied. The observer receives one scalar per pair with no designated supports.
attained_result: At 24 distinctions a full-state symmetry changes exact join eligibility. At 27 there are 48 and 51 possible next joins for two identical state sets. At 36 one presentation can run the whole next round and the other is blocked.
